# NVDA — Quantitative Fundamental Attractiveness Report
**Decision Date: 2026-06-12 | Data through 2026-06-11**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings, and Profitability Trajectory

NVDA's latest reported quarter (Q1 FY2027, period end 2026-04-26) shows extraordinary top-line momentum: revenue of **$81.61B**, up **+43.2% QoQ** from Q3's $57.01B and **+85.2% YoY** from the year-ago quarter's $44.06B. This is not a single-quarter anomaly—the quarterly revenue trajectory from Q1 FY2026 through Q1 FY2027 reads $44.06B → $46.74B → $57.01B → $81.61B, a near-doubling in four quarters.

Net income of **$58.32B** in Q1 implies a net margin of approximately **71.5%**, up from ~56% a year prior. EPS diluted of **$2.39** grew **+214.5% YoY** and **+83.8% QoQ**, indicating operating leverage is expanding rather than compressing. Gross profit of $61.16B on revenue of $81.61B yields a **gross margin of ~74.9%**, consistent with the ratios panel's trailing gross_margin of 0.741. Operating income of $53.54B produces an **operating margin of ~65.6%**, versus ~49% in the year-ago quarter—expansion of roughly 1,600 bps.

**Cash generation** is robust: operating cash flow was **$50.34B** in Q1, up **+112.0% QoQ** and **+83.6% YoY**. Free cash flow is not reported, but OCF at 61.7% of revenue signals the business is converting earnings to cash at a very high rate. The OCF-to-net-income ratio of ~86% is healthy for a capital-light semiconductor platform that is also investing heavily in capex.

**Balance sheet strength** is exceptional. Total equity expanded from $83.84B (Q1 FY2026) to **$195.47B** (Q1 FY2027), more than doubling in one year. Total debt held flat at **$8.47B**. The debt-to-equity ratio stands at **0.043**—effectively negligible leverage. Total assets grew to $259.47B, with liabilities of only $64.00B, giving a liability-to-asset ratio of ~24.7%. This balance sheet can absorb virtually any macro shock or fund any investment initiative without distress.

**TTM note:** The growth panel explicitly flags TTM as incomplete (fiscal gap between Q1→Q3→Q2→Q1 sequences). I therefore do not cite any trailing-twelve-month sums.

## 2. Earnings Quality and Resilience

Earnings quality appears high on several dimensions: (a) operating cash flow substantially exceeds net income in absolute terms ($50.34B vs. $58.32B—close to parity, suggesting minimal accrual distortion given the scale); (b) margins are expanding rather than being propped up by one-time items—the trajectory from ~49% operating margin to ~65.6% over four quarters is structural; (c) the balance sheet carries essentially no debt (D/E = 0.043), eliminating refinancing risk; (d) equity growth is organic (retained earnings-driven), not dilutive—total equity nearly tripled while share count growth appears modest given the EPS trajectory outpacing net income growth on a YoY basis only modestly.

ROE of **0.817** (81.7%) is extraordinarily high, reflecting both profitability and moderate leverage. This is sustainable only as long as growth continues to deploy capital at these returns; any deceleration in AI infrastructure spend would bring ROE down as capital accumulates.

## 3. Valuation vs. Own History

The latest **pe_diluted of 31.3x** (2026-06-11) sits at the **absolute floor** of the 365-day range (30.6–66.8x). Over the past year, NVDA traded at a median PE in the low-to-mid 50s. The current multiple represents a **~40% compression** from the one-year median and sits at roughly half the peak multiple of 66.8x.

**P/B at 25.6x** is also at the bottom of its 365-day range (25.0–57.8x), having compressed from ~52.7x as recently as 2026-05-08. **P/S at 19.7x** reflects the extraordinary revenue scale.

However, context is essential: the PE compression is partly explained by the denominator explosion. EPS grew from $0.76 to $2.39 (+214% YoY), mechanically driving the PE down even if the stock price held steady. The stock at $204.87 is only ~12% above its quarterly-ago level of $183.14, while EPS nearly tripled. The market has not yet re-rated to reflect the new earnings power—at least not on the historical multiple scale.

**Earnings yield of 3.2%** versus the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45% means NVDA's earnings yield actually **trails** the risk-free rate by ~125 bps. This is a meaningful headwind in the current rate regime. For a company growing earnings at >200% YoY, one could argue the yield gap is justified by growth, but it is a quantitative flag.

The **net_margin of 0.63** (63%) and **ROE of 0.817** are near the top of their respective 365-day ranges, confirming that profitability is at peak levels, not recovering from troughs. This is as good as it gets on margin—further expansion is unlikely.

## 4. Price Context vs. Fundamentals

NVDA closed at **$204.87** on 2026-06-11, within a 365-day range of $140.85–$236.54. The stock is ~13% below the high and ~45% above the low. Quarterly returns show modest momentum: +11.9% over the last ~63 trading days (from 2026-03-12's $183.14), preceded by flat-to-negative quarters (-1.0% and +4.3%). Price has essentially consolidated rather than chasing the earnings explosion.

This disconnect—earnings tripling YoY while price gained only ~12% in the latest quarter—is the core of the valuation compression story. The stock has underperformed its own fundamental acceleration, creating a quantitative re-rating opportunity *if* the growth trajectory is believed to be durable.

## 5. Macro and Sentiment Overlays

**Rates:** The 10-year yield at **4.45%** (2026-06-11) has risen ~22 bps over the quarter, and the 2-year at 4.05% is up ~37 bps. The curve remains positively sloped (T10Y2Y = 0.40%), consistent with a non-recessionary environment but one where the Fed (Fed Funds at 3.63%) is not easing aggressively. The 10-year breakeven at 2.29% is contained. Higher long rates compress growth-stock multiples mechanically, which may partly explain the PE compression.

**Volatility:** VIX at **19.44** is elevated (recent spike to 22.22 on 2026-06-10), suggesting market jitters, but has pulled back from the March highs of 31.05. Not extreme but not benign.

**Oil:** WTI at ~$91.58/bbl is elevated and volatile (range ~$85–$114 over the period). This is a cost-of-revenue risk for data center operators (electricity), though NVDA's margins suggest strong pass-through pricing power.

**News sentiment:** Mean score of **0.46** over 90 days with 1,689 articles—moderately positive. Recent readings are choppy (0.875 on June 1, 0.273 on June 10), offering no directional signal. Sentiment is not a thesis driver.

## 6. Strongest Upside and Downside

**Upside:** The PE at 31.3x is at the floor of its history while earnings growth is at its ceiling. If the market re-rates even to a 40x PE (still well below the one-year median of ~52x), the stock could trade above $260 on current EPS—representing ~27% upside from the current price. The earnings trajectory itself is the primary upside catalyst: continued AI infrastructure build-out sustaining >80% revenue growth.

**Downside:** The 74.9% gross margin and 81.7% ROE are at or near unsustainable peaks. Any deceleration in hyperscaler AI capex—a customer concentration risk not quantifiable from this data—would compress margins and earnings simultaneously, triggering a double hit to both EPS and the multiple. The earnings yield below the 10-year Treasury means any further rate rise could compress multiples further. Revenue grew from $44B to $82B in four quarters; sustaining this trajectory requires continued exponential AI demand, which is the central risk.

## 7. Provisional Quantitative Conclusion

NVDA presents a **quantitatively attractive** fundamental profile: best-in-class revenue growth (+85% YoY), expanding margins (74.9% gross, 65.6% operating), fortress balance sheet (D/E = 0.043, $8.47B debt vs. $195.5B equity), and powerful cash generation ($50.3B OCF in a single quarter). Valuation has compressed to multi-year lows on a PE basis (31.3x vs. one-year range of 30.6–66.8x), driven by denominator growth rather than numerator (price) destruction.

The central tension: this is a bet that the earnings trajectory is durable rather than cyclical-peak. Current margins and ROE are at historic highs; the market's reluctance to re-rate upward (PE at floor, earnings yield below risk-free) may reflect rational skepticism about sustainability. However, on purely quantitative fundamentals—growth, profitability, cash flow, balance sheet—NVDA scores at or near the top of any large-cap screen. The valuation discount to its own history, applied to these fundamentals, supports a **positive** provisional view on fundamental attractiveness, with the caveat that durability of the growth inflection is the key swing factor that pure numbers cannot resolve.

---

# NVDA — Qualitative Franchise & Risk Assessment
**Decision date: 2026-06-12 | Analyst: Qualitative**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Nvidia is the undisputed franchise in AI infrastructure. Q1 FY2027 (April 2026) revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY, +20% QoQ) with a $91B Q2 guide (+95% YoY) confirms the company is *accelerating*, not decelerating, at a $360B+ annualized run rate. Data Center revenue of $75.2B (+92% YoY) represents ~92% of total sales, with networking alone surging 199% YoY to $14.8B — evidence that Nvidia sells architecture, not just chips. The new reporting structure (Hyperscale: $37.9B, +115%; AI Clouds/Industrial/Enterprise: $37.4B, +74%) reveals broadening customer demand beyond the top five cloud giants.

**Moat characterization (structural web_search):** Nvidia's competitive advantage rests on three pillars — (1) CUDA software lock-in with 5M+ developers; (2) full-stack integration spanning GPUs, networking (InfiniBand, Spectrum-X), software (TensorRT, NeMo, NIMs), and reference architectures; (3) a fabless asset-light model converting revenue to FCF at extraordinary rates ($48.5B FCF in a single quarter against $1.8B capex). Gross margins of ~75% for a hardware company shipping at this scale reflect structural pricing power. The ~86% data center GPU market share (2025 estimate) may compress toward 70-80% by 2028 as custom ASICs scale, but absolute revenue continues to outpace any competitor's growth.

**Franchise expansion (recent evidence):** At Computex/GTC Taipei (2026-06-01), Nvidia unveiled the Vera CPU (1.8x faster than x86 for agentic workloads), RTX Spark for Windows PCs, Vera Rubin ramping into full production (10x agent throughput vs prior gen), and an expanded DRIVE Hyperion robotaxi platform — collectively opening a $200B standalone CPU TAM. Bank of America's post-CFO-meeting note (2026-06-11) confirmed $20B in Vera CPU sales expected in H2 FY2027 and Vera Rubin featuring 7 chips across 5 racks vs Blackwell's single rack, signaling rising system-level value capture. Nvidia's physical AI business already generates $9B TTM revenue at 50% quarterly growth.

## 2. Recent Developments (Dated)

**Capital allocation inflection (2026-06-11):** Nvidia announced plans to return ~$110B to shareholders over two years, underpinned by a commitment to distribute ≥50% of FCF annually. The quarterly dividend jumped 2,400% from $0.01 to $0.25/share, alongside an $80B buyback authorization. This represents a structural shift in shareholder returns, though the yield remains a modest ~0.5%.

**Customer demand signals (2026-06-11):** Oracle disclosed $55.7B in FY2026 capex (above its $50B guide) with ~$70B planned for FY2027, explicitly benefiting Nvidia as a primary supplier. The SpaceX-Google deal ($920M/month for 110,000 Nvidia GPUs through June 2029) validates that custom chips have not yet displaced Nvidia's GPU ecosystem for large-scale AI compute. Alphabet is raising $80B for AI infrastructure, with Nvidia as a primary beneficiary (2026-06-10).

**Geopolitical/regulatory (2026-05-31):** The U.S. Commerce Department closed the loophole allowing Nvidia AI chip exports to Chinese firms operating overseas. Senator Warren sent a letter probing Nvidia's export-control compliance (response due 2026-06-18), citing criminal cases involving diverted H100/H200 chips. Jensen Huang acknowledged Nvidia's China market share has "dropped to zero." China revenue is now excluded from guidance — growth is primarily supported by non-China customers.

**Macro environment (2026-06-10/11):** May CPI at 4.2% YoY, highest in three years; markets now pricing a potential 25bps rate hike by December. A sharp semiconductor selloff occurred mid-week (SOXL -16% on 2026-06-09) driven by Broadcom's in-line guidance and macro repricing, with NVDA down ~18% from its 52-week high. The selloff appears driven by positioning/valuation reset rather than fundamental demand deterioration.

## 3. Material Risks & Offsets

| Risk | Evidence | Severity | Offset |
|------|----------|----------|--------|
| **Hyperscaler custom silicon** | Amazon, Google, Microsoft designing in-house AI chips; Broadcom's custom ASIC revenue growing 143% YoY | Medium-term structural | Custom chips take 2-3 years to deploy; Nvidia keeps moving the architecture target every 12-18 months; all three hyperscalers remain among Nvidia's largest customers |
| **Concentration** | ~50% of revenue from five customers; 92% from one segment | Structural | New reporting segments (AI Clouds/Industrial/Enterprise: $37.4B) show diversification underway; physical AI/automotive expanding |
| **China export controls** | Market share "dropped to zero"; Senator Warren compliance probe | Real but manageable | China revenue excluded from guidance; growth trajectory unaffected; geopolitical risk is priced in |
| **Valuation sensitivity** | Strong jobs data or rate hikes trigger selloffs; Shiller P/E near dot-com highs | Short-term tactical | NVDA at ~22-23x forward earnings is actually cheap vs peers (AMD ~70x, Marvell ~90x); 34x trailing P/E is below the stock's own historical range |
| **Gross margin pressure** | Rising memory costs; full-stack value capture may face pricing resistance | Low near-term | 75% gross margins sustained; supply-constrained environment preserves pricing power; Vera Rubin platform adds incremental value |
| **Rising CPU emphasis in inference** | GPU-to-CPU ratio shifting from 8:1 (training) to 1:1 (agentic AI) | Medium-term | Nvidia proactively entering CPU market with Vera ($200B TAM), directly offsetting this risk |

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Positive.** The franchise narrative is overwhelmingly supportive of fundamental attractiveness. Nvidia occupies a position rarely seen in technology history — a near-monopoly supplier to an industry-wide capex cycle that is accelerating, not peaking. The structural web_search confirms an 85-92% data center GPU share, software lock-in through CUDA, and a full-stack moat that extends well beyond chip design. Customer commitment is deepening (Blackwell/Vera Rubin through 2027: $1T+ in cumulative orders), and the company is intelligently broadening into CPUs, physical AI, and networking to capture more of the infrastructure value chain.

The recent capital allocation pivot toward $110B in shareholder returns over two years signals management's conviction that the AI infrastructure cycle is durable for 3-5+ years, and that current FCF generation (~$48.5B/quarter) is sustainable enough to fund both growth investment and massive shareholder returns. At ~22x forward earnings, NVDA is the cheapest among major AI semiconductor peers — a notable anomaly for the dominant franchise in a structural growth market.

Key qualifiers: (1) The business is extraordinarily concentrated — five customers, one segment — which amplifies downside if any single customer pivots to custom silicon or if AI capex decelerates sharply; (2) the China compliance probe adds regulatory noise; and (3) macro headwinds (inflation at 4.2%, potential rate hikes) create valuation risk independent of fundamentals.
